hook: A short file about a silent heap of gears that has to be kept rusting in seawater. Read it as a mood piece; much of the unease comes from the precise, oddly specific procedures. The tags link it to the Broken God, but you need no background to enjoy it.
whyItMatters: It is a compact way into the clockwork imagery the broken-god tag points to. A machine that grows by swallowing metal, and draws people toward it with noises only they can hear, is a strong and simple hook. It also shows how a featured article can work with just a few paragraphs and some well-chosen loose threads.
thingsToNotice:
The central contradiction is the best touch: the object makes no sound at all, yet people who stay near it start hearing grinding and clicking that gets louder and only quiets when they throw metal into it. At the end of that road they throw themselves in, are crushed almost instantly, and the body is usually pulled inside where it cannot be recovered; hence the rule that staff who report hearing things are examined and may be locked away for good.

The recovery notes do a lot with little: a mile-wide circle scrubbed of every scrap of metal, the machine sitting at its exact centre already sunk in seawater, and a small town nearby that had been empty for years. Rust is the containment, so decay is the one thing keeping it still, and the moment it was lifted out and the rust flaked off it began to move. The final lines point to SCP-271, SCP-217 and a separate interview without explaining any of them.

related.note: Played on a loop during recovery, it slowed the machine enough for staff to approach.
The file orders anyone possibly contaminated by it to be kept away from this machine.
